title: Install auth token is persisted without explicit restrictive file permissions
reasoning: The persisted install auth state includes installToken, userId, and installId, but saveInstallAuthStateToDisk writes the JSON file with default process umask permissions and no platform credential store or explicit mode. On machines or packaged environments with permissive umasks or shared userData directories, this can expose a reusable install credential to other local users or processes.
recommendation: Persist install auth through the OS credential store where available, or at minimum write the file with restrictive permissions such as mode 0o600 and ensure the parent directory is not group/world-readable. Avoid logging token-bearing payloads and document the migration/security behavior.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included tests assert filesystem mode, credential-store usage, or migration behavior for install-auth.json.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a focused test that saves install auth state using a temp userData path and asserts the resulting file mode is owner-read/write only on POSIX platforms, with an explicit Windows expectation if ACL checks are implemented separately.
minimumFixScope: saveInstallAuthStateToDisk and associated install-auth persistence tests.
